blocks.text: Condo buildings in Central Abbotsford
Mahogany at Mill Lake — 2180 Gladwin Road
A 27-storey concrete tower of 152 suites by Quantum Properties, beside Mill Lake (developer/construction source).
Regency Park — 3170 Gladwin Road (listings also use 3150 Gladwin Road for units in the same complex)

Built 1990, 188 units. The directory records restrictions as: age restrictions, pets not allowed, rentals not allowed — but: any long-term rental-restriction bylaw has been unenforceable province-wide since Nov 24, 2022, so the rental line in the directory is outdated law even if the bylaw text still exists. Listings describe it as a 55+ concrete high-rise with indoor pool, sauna, fitness centre and guest suites.
Montvue — 33820 South Fraser Way (Historic Downtown)

Two 5-storey mixed-use buildings by Parcel7 Homes with homes above ground-floor commercial, completed in 2025, per the project architect, Keystone Architecture, which counts 90 residential units. Presale-directory sources describe the same project as two 6-storey wood-frame buildings with 110 condominiums and 10 retail units — the unit count and storey count conflict between sources.
The Mason at The Rail District — 2771 Montrose Avenue (Historic Downtown)

A 6-storey mixed-use building by Infinity Properties with 93 condominiums (643–1,152 sq ft, 1-bedroom to 2-bedroom + den), up to nine ground-level retail units and two levels of underground parking; it is the first condo building in The Rail District master plan on the 19-acre former Clayburn Brick Plant site, and it completed in spring 2026.
College Park — 33728 King Road
Built 1998; amenities listed are elevator, exercise centre, guest suite, in-suite laundry and storage.
Natura — off Gladwin Road, behind the Regency Park complex
Built 2022, with air conditioning in most units (local agent review, secondary source).
Upper Montrose — Historic Downtown
Built 2020, with air conditioning and large 900+ sq ft 2-bedroom floor plans (local agent review, secondary source).
Aria — 33538 Cottage Lane
is a new rental apartment building (pre-leasing, move-ins anticipated January 15, 2027), not strata condos for sale.

items.t: "Central Abbotsford" is the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name used in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.

The City's own commercial study describes the City Centre as roughly bordered by Peardonville Road and Mill Lake to the south, Ware Street, Mill Lake Road and Horn Street to the east, Parkview Street and Tims Street to the west, and a line roughly parallel to George Ferguson Way and Maclure Road to the north, centred on South Fraser Way.

South Fraser Way is the commercial backbone; other main streets in plan material are George Ferguson Way, McCallum Road, Clearbrook Road, Ware Street and Old Yale Road, with Highway 1 interchanges at McCallum and Clearbrook.

Where the condo stock concentrates: (1) the Gladwin Road / Mill Lake corridor south of South Fraser Way — the area's towers and low-rises (Mahogany, Regency Park, Natura) all sit on or just off Gladwin; (2) Historic Downtown around Montrose Avenue, South Fraser Way and the Rail District lands between Pine Street and Morey Avenue (Montvue, The Mason, Upper Montrose); (3) the McCallum Road / King Road edge by the University of the Fraser Valley (College Park).

Bourquin Exchange, the central transit exchange, is in the area, and BC Transit routes serving Abbotsford include 1 (Highstreet/UFV), 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), 4 (Saddle/Montrose), 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), 12 (UFV/Bourquin), 17 (Industrial/Bourquin), 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford) and 31 (Abbotsford/Mission).
There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Abbotsford.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Abbotsford condos

items.t: Abbotsford replaced its Official Community Plan in December 2025. After more than two years of work, Council adopted the new Abbotsforward 2050 OCP in December 2025 (public hearing November 25, 2025); it emphasizes more apartments, townhouses and SSMUH in priority areas and enables the 37,185 units the City's 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report targets over 20 years. Condo buyers should read designations under the new OCP, not the 2016 plan most older pages still describe.

The Rail District is a 10-to-12-year build-out, not a finished neighbourhood. The 19-acre former Clayburn Brick Plant site between Pine Street and Morey Avenue is planned as five neighbourhoods in nine phases over 10 to 12 years; The Mason (completed spring 2026) is only the first condo building, and the community amenity building, The Station, serves all five planned neighbourhoods. Early buyers are buying into a construction zone with an amenity payoff at the end.

Downtown's main intersection is being rebuilt. The City is realigning Montvue Avenue — removing the single-lane connection to Essendene Avenue, connecting Montvue directly to West Railway Street, and turning the closed street section into West Railway Plaza, a public gathering/market space — as part of the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan.

The OCP growth direction adds a new centre east of downtown: Abbotsforward 2050 states a new mixed-use centre between the hospital and Mill Lake Park and a Primary Transit Corridor along South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road — the corridor the Gladwin Road condo cluster already sits beside.

items.t: City zoning/plans: Historic Downtown's Urban 2 – Ground Oriented designation enables rowhouses, townhouses, multiplexes and duplexes.
GST on new townhomes (Rail District phases): 5% GST on new construction, not resales. GST New Housing Rebate: 36%, max $6,300, $350K–$450K phase-out.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Abbotsford townhomes

items.t: Abbotsford replaced its Official Community Plan in December 2025. Abbotsforward 2050 (public hearing November 25, 2025) emphasizes more apartments, townhouses and SSMUH in priority areas and enables the 37,185 units the City's 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report targets over 20 years.
The King Road cluster's sub-area label is unreliable in feeds: the same Argyle address (34248 King Road) appears as Poplar, Abbotsford East and Central Abbotsford in different listings.

Downtown's main intersection is being rebuilt: the City is realigning Montvue Avenue — removing the single-lane connection to Essendene Avenue, connecting Montvue directly to West Railway Street, and turning the closed section into West Railway Plaza — as part of the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan, on the Rail District townhouses' own street network.

The OCP's growth arrow points at the hospital–Mill Lake gap: Abbotsforward 2050 states a new mixed-use centre between the hospital and Mill Lake Park and a Primary Transit Corridor along South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road — the corridor the George Ferguson townhouse cluster sits beside.

Federal Housing Accelerator money is spent, not pending: the City was approved for up to $25.6 million in HAF money and reported in October 2026 that all HAF initiatives are complete, with multi-family permitting above expectations — part of why so much new mid-rise and townhouse product landed in the core at once.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

298 condos sold in Central Abbotsford with a median price of $390,000 (the middle half sold between $325,000 and $453,750), taking a median of 36 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $414 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $426 a month. 105 townhomes sold in Central Abbotsford with a median price of $620,000 (the middle half sold between $540,000 and $692,000), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 97.7% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $375 per square foot, a median year built of 1992 and a median strata fee of $381 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 236 condos and townhomes listed in Central Abbotsford. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Central Abbotsford?

faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Central Abbotsford had a sales ratio of 18%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
faq.q: Is Central Abbotsford a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 209 condos and townhomes sold in Central Abbotsford over those 5 months, out of 407 in all of Abbotsford.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Central Abbotsford from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — every residential rental-restriction bylaw in BC became unenforceable on November 24, 2022, even if the strata has never amended the bylaw text. Short-term rentals can still be banned by bylaw, and a 55+ age bylaw (like Regency Park's) still governs who may live in the unit, tenant or owner.
faq.q: The building's bylaws say "no rentals." Can I still rent out my condo?

faq.a: The fee split between the operating fund and the CRF is on the Form B, which also states the current CRF balance; since November 1, 2023 the CRF contribution must be at least 10% of the operating fund.
faq.q: What does the strata fee actually cover, and how do I check it?

faq.a: Read the depreciation report through the Form B: since July 1, 2024 every strata with 5+ lots must have one on a five-year cycle, with a 30-year cost projection and three CRF funding models that show whether the plan is "pay as you go," increased fees, or special levies.
faq.q: How do I know if a big special levy is coming?

faq.a: It tracks building form: The Mason has two levels of underground parking. The specific stall and locker assigned to a unit are stated on the Form B — never assume from the listing.
faq.q: Is parking underground or surface, and is storage included?

faq.a: The strata's master policy deductible — especially the water-damage deductible — can be charged back to an owner whose unit causes a loss, so buyers line up their own unit-owner policy against the deductible amount shown in the strata documents.
faq.q: What insurance risk do condo buyers miss?

faq.a: Strata in every known case — Oakhurst Park (NWS1894), Summerset Place, Willband Creek Estates, Canterbury Gate and The Abby Townhome Series all carry strata title or published strata fees.
faq.q: Is a central townhouse strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: Residency, not ownership: an under-55 buyer can own, but may not live in the unit unless exempt (younger spouse/partner, legacy resident, live-in caregiver, defined children — Regulation 7.01, expanded May 1, 2023). The bylaw is the only legal age bylaw in BC strata law.
faq.q: Three of these complexes are 55+. What does that actually restrict?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, the strata cannot rely on a rental-restriction bylaw — those are void since Nov 24, 2022 — but the tenant must still meet the 55+ bylaw or an exemption, and short-term rentals can still be banned.
faq.q: Can I rent out a unit in a 55+ townhouse complex?
What did condos in Central Abbotsford sell for?
faq.a: The median condo sale in Central Abbotsford was $390,000, across 298 sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Central Abbotsford?
faq.a: Typical time on the market was 36 days. At the median, sale prices were 97.0% of list, and 6% of sales closed above list (November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
